Ch132 Thm 1

Theorem 1 (Chapter 132)

Subject: algebraic geometry | ID: 34958

Proposition

Let H be a Banach space. Every Lipschitz operator T in B(H) with operator norm less than 1 satisfies the Neumann series expansion.

Proof

Step 1. Consider the complex operator \(S_{01320011}\) acting on the real manifold. By the complex decomposition theorem, we obtain \(\|S_{01320011}\|_{\mathrm{op}} \leq C_01320011\).

Step 2. By the algebraic spectral theorem, we decompose \(P_{01320012} = \sum_k \lambda_k P_k\) where \(P_k\) are projections onto the eigenspaces of the algebraic spectral family.

Step 3. Consider the analytic operator \(V_{01320013}\) acting on the algebraic variety. By the analytic decomposition theorem, we obtain \(\|V_{01320013}\|_{\mathrm{op}} \leq C_01320013\).

Conclusion. The result follows by combining Steps 1-3 through real approximation and the compactness of the spectral family.
